resources.string: Keeps Home in front on TVs that will not let you change the default home app. It reads nothing on the screen.
Installed from the APK alone, Home opens, but the Home button, power-on and wake still go to the TV’s own launcher.
Or set it up from a computer (recommended)
Scan with your phone for this TV’s command, ready to paste or hand to an assistant.
No inputs found on this TV
No networks yet. The TV is still looking, or its location is off.
The TV’s own keyboard opens for this; its Done key joins the network.
The TV would not join it. Its own network page can.
A network with a password asks for it; one the TV knows, or one with none, joins as it stands. Android 10 lets only the system add a network.
Move with the arrows · Press OK when done
Move with the arrows, or tap a spot · Press OK or tap the app when done
Select an app to put it back on Home
No weather yet. It loads once the TV is online.
Located from the network. If that is wrong, scan the code to set your city.
City set on your phone. Scan the code to change it.
Aerial films that move behind Home. They play while the Dock is in front and hold the frame you are on when you go down to the apps.
Bing’s photo of the day, new every day.
A different photo of yours each day.
Your photo. Scan the code to send more from your phone.
Light taken from the selected app’s artwork.
Not chosen yet, so it follows the wallpaper: films with the aerial wallpaper, photos with a picture. Choose one to keep it.
Set up from a phone or computer
Scan the code, or open the address in a computer’s browser, to send photos and videos, change icons and set the city. Both must be on the TV’s network.
Connect the TV to a network to set it up from a phone or computer.
Tip: press Back on the Dock to start the screen saver.
What Back does on the Dock. Turn it off if it gets pressed by accident; the screen saver still starts on its own.
Auto plays the best this TV can show. With 4K Dolby Vision chosen the TV may go black for a moment as it switches. Choose 1080p if films often skip.
The side the date, lunar day and time sit on.
Large puts the date over big digits. Two large modules sit one on each side.
The side the weather sits on.
Large puts the day’s range on the top line and the place and humidity beside bigger degrees.
Names under the app in focus, as on Apple TV, or under every app.
One Row keeps the Dock alone, low on the screen, leaving more room for the wallpaper. Two Rows stands another row of apps above it; press down for the rest.
A plate of frosted glass under the Dock, as on Apple TV, or the apps straight on the wallpaper.
Sounds as focus moves, on select and on Back, as on Apple TV.
The TV’s own key sounds, as in its menus. Silent if key sounds are off in the TV’s settings.
Apps hidden from Home are kept here, to put back. With a passcode set, it asks first.
A white frame around the selected app, easy to spot from across the room.
As on Apple TV out of the box: the selected app only lifts.
Reduced draws plain panels and drops the sheen and parallax, and keeps the screen at 60 Hz: for TVs that stutter.
This TV has little memory or an older Android, so Auto uses Reduced.
Switch to this input when the TV turns on or wakes. The Home button still brings you back. To start on an app instead, press and hold it on Home and choose Open When TV Turns On.
Pinned inputs appear as tiles at the front of Home; select one to switch straight to it. Long-press a tile to rearrange or remove it.
Your apps, layout, wallpaper and settings stay as they are.
Scan with a phone to see how to update: copy the install command, or hand it to an assistant.
Cannot install? Scan with a phone for other ways to update.
The installer is open: confirm the update there. When it is done, choose Done to come back with every setting kept.
Allow this app to install apps in the settings that just opened, then come back and choose Download and Install again.
This TV needs storage access to save the update. Allow the file permission, then choose Download and Install again.
The download did not finish. Check the network and try again, or update with the command below.
This TV does not let apps install other apps. Update with the command below.
This app on this TV is signed differently from the official one, so it cannot be updated over.
No newer version out there yet. Try again in a while.
Asked before the TV’s settings open and before hidden apps come back.
Use the number keys or the keypad below.
Four digits. Keep it somewhere safe: if it is forgotten, only a computer over ADB can clear it.
The two passcodes differ. Set one again.
Digits come from the number keys or the keypad. Arrows are four presses of the arrow keys, and a child watching sees nothing to copy.
Press the arrow keys four times: up, down, left or right.
Press the arrow keys four times. Keep the order somewhere safe: forgotten, only a computer over ADB can clear it.
How many apps fit across a row, in folders too. Six shows more at a glance; four makes them larger.
With One Row, the row below shows a sliver above the Dock as a hint that there is more. Off keeps it out of sight until you press down.
Don’t Open When TV Turns On
%1$s will open when the TV turns on
%1$s will open when the TV turns on, instead of %2$s
%1$s will no longer open when the TV turns on
Add MP4 or MOV films from the phone page. Plays offline; photos are shown when no film can play.
The screen saver that came with the TV (Xiaomi’s pictures, for one). Home shows none of its own.
Your own videos, sent from the phone, silent and one after another. They move like the aerial films and hold the frame you are on.
Your own video, sent from the phone, silent and on a loop. It moves like the aerial films and holds the frame you are on.
This input’s live picture behind Home, without sound; open the input for sound. Going down to the apps, it gives way to a frosted background.
On Idle: plays after 10 seconds on the Dock; a key stops it. Always: keys do not stop it, and it is shaded a little; it stops when you go down to the apps.
The clock over the film and photo screen savers. It drifts a little now and then, so nothing stays on the same pixels.
Home speaks its own language. The date, the clock and the weather follow it; Follow TV keeps the TV’s.
The weather takes turns through these towns, ten seconds each, like a departure board.
No cities listed for this province.
How long Home waits with the remote untouched before the TV sleeps. Left and right take a minute off, or add one: 1 to 30 minutes.

Writes the TV\’s quick-standby mode so Mi Home keeps working and wake is instant while the TV is off. Standby draws a little more power. On TVs that ignore the setting, pick it in the TV\’s own settings.
Turning this on needs the write-secure-settings permission: run tools/install.sh once over ADB (see README).
Scan to open the settings page: send your own photos, change an icon or a name.
Want your own photos on Home? Scan with your phone and send one over.
No network: connect the TV to Wi-Fi or Ethernet first.
